text:
mira: Quick sync — we need to pick a path for next sprint: 'brand anchoring' (unique UX + premium positioning) vs 'compatibility shim' (fast parity with competitor behavior). ACME pilot is pushing for shim; several inbound RFPs expect parity. Decision needed by EOD Thu so sales can respond.

eduardo: What are the engineering cost deltas? numbers please.

sanjay: From design POV, brand anchoring gives us an opportunity to showcase Redwood's predictability. But it takes extra polish on error states.

julia: Sales: ACME & BetaCorp both said "parity first" in calls. If we don't ship a shim, we lose pilot close this quarter.

eduardo: Rough back-of-envelope: shim = ~2 sprints (infra + compatibility layer + tests). anchoring = ~4 sprints (design polish, rollout controls, extra observability).

mira: Key constraints: 1) time-to-close ACME (2 weeks), 2) not regressing latency/SLOs, 3) maintain cost per token within target.

sanjay: Proposal: do a minimal shim that covers the top 3 parity behaviors ACME cares about, but behind a feature flag and branded UX default. That preserves positioning while buying time.

julia: If we can promise a behind-flag parity in 2 sprints and a brand-anchored default later, ACME is likely to sign a short pilot. I can get them to sign a conditional LOI.

eduardo: Technically feasible. Suggest split work: infra + routing compatibility (sprint 1), tests + canary (sprint 2). Anchored UX in subsequent sprint. Need a rollback plan.

mira: Launch criteria (for parity shim canary):
- parity flag can be toggled per-tenant
- latency regression < 10% vs baseline
- rolling canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automatic rollback on errors
- end-to-end tests for top-10 ACME prompts

sanjay: I'll draft the minimal UI copy/consent flow for the feature flag. Keep it subtle so product messaging still leads with Redwood differentiators.

julia: Sales note: Negotiable ask — ACME accepts feature-flag parity if we commit to brand-anchored GA within 8 weeks. That timeline aligns with design's 2-sprint uplift.

eduardo: Ops checklist snippet:
```
- add routing rule for parity shim
- expose per-tenant toggle in admin UI
- telemetry: per-flag latency, token counts, error rate
- automated rollback hook on 5xx spike or >15% latency regression
```

mira: Risk callouts:
- parity shim increases surface area for bugs (compat edge cases)
- shipping shim may set customer expectations for parity across other models
- delaying anchor UX could make marketing messaging less distinct for GA

julia: Proposed negotiation language for ACME: "We will enable a parity compatibility flag for pilot, with an explicit timeline for brand-anchored GA and SLA uplift." I can draft.

eduardo: What about metrics to accept the pilot? sales asks for a success definition.

mira: Pilot acceptance metrics (suggested):
- error-free sample interactions >= 98% over a 7-day window
- median latency within 15% of baseline
- no regression in token cost above 5% for pilot traffic
- positive qualitative feedback from ACME success team

sanjay: Sounds good. Also request a short prompt set from ACME — we'll use it for gated e2e tests.

julia: I'll get the prompt set and the LOI language.

eduardo: I'll scope the infra tasks and add to sprint board. Will need 1 senior infra and 1 backend for 2 sprints.

mira: OK action items:
- julia: LOI + prompt set by Wed EOD
- sanjay: minimal UI copy + consent flow by Wed EOD
- eduardo: infra task list + sprint estimate by Tue noon
- mira: finalize launch criteria doc and publish to Console checklist by Thu EOD

julia: acked.

sanjay: ack.

eduardo: ack.

deploy-bot: Reminder: new feature-flag toggles require infra owner approval before canary rollout. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/feature-flags

mira: Thanks all — leaning toward the hybrid path (shim behind flag, anchor for GA). We'll reconvene Wed after estimates. :thumbsup:
